notes.text: This particle alternates with lɁmr in OfA, thus showing that it is a colloquial shortening of the latter. See bibliography in Dictionary of the North-West Semitic Inscriptions, Brill, 1995">DNWSI. Some Syriac writers/translators, in quoting earlier writers, use the particle only in meaning 2 while citing direct citations without it, as in the cited example. The point being that the particle marks a different authorial point of view. In poetry, the particle, normally "enclitic" after the first sense unit, can come elsewhere in the quote, when metrical considerations require it to be so, even at the very end of an extended quotation.

notes.text: Note especially that Syriac ܠܐ ܗܘܐ "not" does not have a reference to past time. Given that in the earliest texts simple "not" is prefixed to its verb, it is probable that the later common spelling with final aleph reflects the interjectional usage with a clear final glottal as often heard in Arabic. One might then distinguish lexically between original lā_ "not" and lāɁ" "no!" in Northwest Semitic. The Syriac ܠܐ ܗܘܐ is replaced by ܠܘ in later texts, for which see s.v. lɁw, lw adv.
